title: American accent detection for real-world speech
summary: Buyers pay for American English. Accentus checks the accent first, on real conversation and phone audio. In real conversation it rejects 2% of Americans, and it names the accent it heard. Now in closed beta.
body_markdown:
## Why we built it


Buyers pay for American English. Contributors around the world record it for us, on phones, in real rooms, in the middle of a conversation. We could not listen to every clip, and the models we tried rejected too many real Americans or let too many non-Americans through.


So we built our own.


## Built for the way people talk


Accent detection is usually tested on one person reading one paragraph in a quiet room. Real speech is messier. People interrupt, trail off, laugh and change pace. They call from a kitchen, over a line that drops frames.


So we built Accentus for conversation, and we tested it on calls from people held out of training.


Those are two-person calls, each speaker on their own track, with at least 30 seconds of speech each. Accentus rejected 5 of 233 Americans and 200 of 216 speakers from the four groups, and it named the right group for 190 of 197. On a phone line it rejected 2 of 217 Americans. The full results are on the[model page](https://www.luel.ai/lab/models/accentus) .


## Against ten other systems


We ran the same calls through ten other systems: open accent models, and AI models from Google, Meta, Alibaba and Thinking Machines. Accentus rejected the fewest Americans: 5 of 233. The next best rejected 14, and Gemini 3.8 Flash rejected 50 of 212. It came out lowest on every channel we tested: the original call, a noisy room, VoIP and a phone line.


Some systems stopped more of the other speakers. Every one of them did it by rejecting at least one American in five. The full comparison is on the[US Accent Benchmark](https://www.luel.ai/lab/benchmarks/us-accent) .


## Pass, Review or Reject


Accentus does not return a percentage. It returns one of three answers. Pass means it heard an American accent. Reject means it did not, and when the speaker is from one of the four groups it knows, it names the group. Review means a person should listen. A noisy room or a bad line goes there instead of being guessed at. Under 10 seconds of speech there is no answer at all.


That is the point. A model that puts a score on every clip has to be trusted on every clip. Accentus says yes, says no, or asks a person, and only the last one costs anyone time.


## What it unlocks


Accentus checks first. It can gate new American English recordings, turning a Reject away or sending it to a reviewer. It can audit recordings already approved as American. And when a speaker is not American, it names the accent it heard, which is the start of listing that recording correctly instead of throwing it away.


That is the bigger idea. The hardest data to find is real human behaviour, recorded well. Our contributor network collects it in the conditions people live in, and a model is only useful if it works on that data.


## What comes next


This is a first release, and it is strongest on conversation. It names four groups today. On a scripted read, a put-on American accent can still pass, so a Pass on a read-aloud paragraph should not stand on its own. About one American in ten goes to Review in conversation, and one in five in a noisy room. That is work for a person. Next we are adding more groups and tightening scripted reads.


## Try it


Accentus is in closed beta.[Request access](https://www.luel.ai/request?model=accentus) and tell us what American English audio you want checked.
